text:
The snapshot looks like mid-2021. Industrial production is up 16% YoY, which reflects the base effect from April 2020. Unemployment is 5.8%, which matches May or June 2021. Headline CPI is 4.93% and core is 3.8%, which is close to the May 2021 figures (5.0% headline, 3.8% core). The 10-year yield at 1.49% fits June 2021, and the 20y+ Treasury return of +4.4% for the month fits that too, since yields fell in June. Gold fell 6.9% in June 2021, which also fits.

Headline CPI of 4.93% is a little off from the published 5.0% for May, but may reflect rounding or a different series. Unemployment of 5.8% was the May and June figure (June was 5.9%, May 5.8%). Because of publication lags, the latest data at the end of June would show May CPI, which is 5.0%, and May unemployment at 5.8%. That fits June 2021.

Payrolls averaged 540k over three months, which matches April through June, though the June jobs report came out in July. So the snapshot is most likely June 2021.
